obligation: G110/G111 -- does isolated-family time predict what a retile buys?
method: Revert each landed retile via its env knob and measure BOTH the isolated family delta and the production token delta, paired, 2 runs per arm. Transfer = d_token / d_iso.
prerequisite_defect_found_and_fixed: The three revert knobs DID NOT WORK. Every site filtered the parsed value with `v.is_power_of_two() && (32..=1024).contains(v)`, which REJECTS 0, so the documented `HAWKING_ROPE_TG=0` fell through to `.unwrap_or(256)` -- the fast path -- and the `if tg > 0` branch selecting the old kernel was UNREACHABLE. Seven sites across three knobs. Three commit messages document those knobs as the way to revert and none of them reverted. A first attempt at this very experiment produced nonsense transfer coefficients (8.85, 1.63, 3.47) because of it. Fixed to `*v == 0 || (...)`; proof: rope_cache_16 goes 0.1369 -> 1.5880 ms with the knob at 0, an 11.6x revert that matches the pre-retile census figure of 1.5626.
finding: TRANSFER DEPENDS ON FAMILY SIZE. The three families above 1 ms transfer at 1.01-1.23, i.e. essentially 1:1 given a 0.28 ms noise floor on ~1.5 ms deltas. The 0.33 ms family transfers 0.00.
correction: This CORRECTS the generalisation I drew from argmax alone, that isolated-family time is 'a ranking signal, not a budget'. That was one case over-generalised. It IS a budget for families above about 1 ms -- all three tested transfer fully -- and argmax is the exception, not the rule.
hypothesis_for_argmax: argmax is a single dispatch at the very END of the token, so its cost may overlap the host-side tail rather than sitting on the GPU critical path, whereas rope, rmsnorm and dn_rmsnorm are mid-token with dependents behind them. Stated as a hypothesis; not tested.
actionable_remainder: Of the 5.869 ms non-GEMV wall, the attackable part is what sits above the ~1 ms transfer threshold: gated_delta_48 at 1.9795 ms, and possibly mha_16 at 0.5266. rearrange_48 (0.3511) and argmax (0.3343) are in the range argmax proved unrecoverable.
